claim: A March 2026 Forbes article whose entire premise is that few creators earn meaningful income never quantifies that claim anywhere in its text — no percentage, sample size, survey, or year is given for the central assertion.
stance_target: The proposition that trade-press statements about creator income concentration rest on measurable evidence
scope_conditions: Forbes contributor column by Meggen Harris, published 23 March 2026, updated 25 March 2026; contributor content is explicitly labelled 'independent expert analyses', not Forbes editorial reporting; body partially truncated by a paywall interstitial
quoted_support: More than 200 million people worldwide now identify as creators yet only a small percentage earn enough to treat it as a full-time business. Most make little to nothing.

claim: The article demonstrates aggregate-vs-distribution laundering in its purest form: a market-size figure and a creator-population figure are placed adjacently, each sourced to a vendor or VC blog, with the distribution between them asserted only qualitatively.
stance_target: The methodological objection that creator-economy reporting substitutes total market size for distributional evidence
scope_conditions: The $100B+ figure links to Influencer Marketing Hub, a vendor; the 200 million creators figure links to SignalFire, a venture capital firm's blog; neither link is to a survey with a stated sample or methodology
quoted_support: While the creator economy is now estimated to exceed $100 billion globally the number of people earning meaningful, consistent income within it is far smaller—and far more specific—than most people assume.

claim: The article's OnlyFans earnings-concentration claim is sourced to a commercial OnlyFans management agency's blog rather than to any platform disclosure or independent analysis.
stance_target: The reliability of cross-platform concentration claims repeated in mainstream business press
scope_conditions: Hyperlink text points to infloww.com, an OnlyFans creator-management vendor, with a nested reference to businessofapps.com statistics aggregation
quoted_support: While billions have been paid out to creators, earnings are heavily concentrated among a small percentage of top accounts.

claim: The article contains no attrition data, no survival-rate data, no income-distribution percentiles, and no time-to-first-income evidence, despite being one of the highest-ranking search results for creator earnings questions.
stance_target: The finding that high-visibility creator-economy coverage is systematically absent of the quantities researchers actually need
scope_conditions: Full text reviewed (1,455 words as fetched, including paywall interstitial); audited absence rather than a positive finding
quoted_support: Access creates participation while structure creates income.
